requirement: `habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.
rationale:
**Implementation**

- `render_evidence_table` in `src/markdown.rs` (lines 1–28) is the one renderer. It takes `(name cell, label)` rows. It computes each column's width as the maximum of the header text and the cell contents. It pads both columns with `{:<width$}` for the header, the `---` separator and every row. It is marked `{impl}` for this requirement and for `status_table_alignment`.
- `habeas status` (`status_markdown_with_options`, `src/commands.rs`) builds rows of ``format!("`{name}` ({noun})")`` plus `evidence.state().label()`. It passes them to `render_evidence_table`, and the call site is marked `{impl}`.
- The mdBook index (`DetailPlan::populate`, `src/index.rs`) builds rows with linked name cells, `[`name`](href) (noun)`, plus `evidence.state().label()`. It passes them to the same `render_evidence_table`, and the call site is marked `{impl}`.
- Both callers take their labels from the single `EvidenceState::label()` (`src/index.rs`, lines 248–270). Both outputs therefore show identical state labels.
- The requirement allows callers to select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells. The status command filters by glob, `--all` and `--verbose`. The index uses all planned detail pages with link cells.
- Nothing in the marked code goes beyond the requirement. Width is measured in bytes (`.len()`), which is fine for the ASCII identifiers and labels used here.

**Tests**

- `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (`src/index.rs`, marked `{test}`) covers the index side. It checks linked name cells, with the kind label, for five definitions. It checks the label for each of the Valid, Determination false, Invalid and Missing states. It checks that all table lines have identical pipe positions, so the columns are aligned.
- `status_tables_align_each_column_to_its_widest_cell` (`tests/commands.rs`, marked `{test}` for `status_table_alignment`) covers the status side. It runs both `status` and `status --all`. It checks pipe alignment, one space of padding, column width equal to the widest cell, and the header and separator rows.
- Both outputs go through one function, so the two tests together cover the shared behaviour. There is no test that compares the two outputs directly, and no empty-table case. I judged that acceptable because sharing the function is structural, and the empty-row case is handled in `status` by not emitting a table.
